To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rules, regulations and requirements of institutions are formulated and enforced to meet normative belief criteria, and are formulated and enforced in ways that are consistent with technological and ecological criteria, and that these three criteria interact in complex ways.

the characteristics of institutions are: (1) the rules, regulations and requirements are formulated and enforced by social actors, (2) institutions have a technological and ecological component in addition to a social component, and (3) institutions are open systems, not closed systems.

1) institutions are social systems that are open, endogenous, and not self-organized, 2) the main activity inside institutions is rule formulation and enforcement, 3) the main function of rules is to regulate the social activities of persons as social actors and service providers, and 4) the key concepts of social science are the concepts of institutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characteristics of complex systems, the theoretical development of those systems, and the analysis of the systems as they exist in the real world.
the analysis of the complex systems characteristics and theoretical development that is necessary for the analysis of institutions.
the characteristics and theoretical development that are necessary for the analysis of the internal operations of institutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

institutional analysis requires the recognition and observation of rules, regulations and requirements, which are formulated to satisfy normative belief, technical, and ecological criteria, and which are enforced in a manner consistent with those criteria.
institutions are open systems that are self-organized and self-regulated by the formulation and enforcement rules, regulations, requirements, and other social activities.

the analysis of institutions must be conducted by modeling the rules, regulations and requirements which are consistent with normative beliefs and technological and ecological criteria, and that the concepts of closed systems and self-organization are irrelevant for the analysis of institutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
institutions can be modeled as open systems, with endogenous and exogenous inputs, and with a self-organized process for the formulation and enforcement, of rules, regulations and requirements.
institutions are open systems that are endogenous and self-organized, but they are also designed and managed by social actors, and are subject to external forces.
the analysis of institutions must be based on a model that includes all three criteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is necessary to observe the rules, regulations and requirements that are formulated and enforced by institutions, and to model them as being consistent with the normativity, technology, and ecology of the institution.
it is necessary to include all three criteria in the analysis of institutional processes.
the analysis inside institutions requires the use of a theoretical model that is based on the characteristics of the institutions being analyzed.
